action: Lockout then regrease with the recommended amount then restart and verify against baseline
tradeoff_explained_by_coach: Cheap and fast. Works only if the bearing is not yet damaged, so verification after restart is mandatory.
Safe and permanent, but more downtime and parts cost than needed if caught early.

action: Keep running and schedule a repair with monitoring
tradeoff_explained_by_coach: Acceptable only with manager sign-off and close monitoring. A dry bearing can seize quickly.
Never service a running or energized machine. The fix is right but the method can injure you.

action: Lockout then purge excess grease then run-in and check a-Peak and a-RMS return to baseline
tradeoff_explained_by_coach: Removes the cause. Over-greasing creates heat from churning; the bearing needs a run-in period.
Solves it but wastes a healthy bearing and adds downtime.
The classic mistake: it makes overheating worse. Always confirm the pattern before repeating last time's fix.

action: Restart without comparing readings to baseline
tradeoff_explained_by_coach: You cannot claim a fix without verification. Compare V-RMS, a-Peak and temperature with the healthy baseline.
